title: Sooryavanshi, 15, Smashes Fastest List A Century and Double Century in 204-Run Blitz
excerpt: The India A opener reached 100 in 28 balls and 200 in 52 — both List A records — and hit a record 28 sixes as India A chased 250 in 14.2 overs against the UAE in Doha.
body:
• Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates in Doha, hitting the fastest century (28 balls) and the fastest double century (52 balls) in List A cricket history.
  • His 28 sixes are a List A record for a single innings, breaking D'Arcy Short's mark of 23; the previous fastest double century, by Chad Bowes, took 103 balls.
  • India A chased down the UAE's 249 for 8 in just 14.2 overs, winning by seven wickets with 214 balls to spare in the Asia Cup Rising Stars.
  • The UAE total rested on Harpreet Singh's 130 off 144 balls; Arshad Khan took 4 for 43 for India A.

India A beat the United Arab Emirates by seven wickets in Doha on Tuesday, and the result was the least remarkable part of the match. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15 years old, made 204 from 53 balls — an innings that broke the List A records for the fastest century, the fastest double century and the most sixes in an innings, and carried India A to 254 for 3 in 14.2 overs in pursuit of 250.

An innings of records

Sooryavanshi reached his fifty in 16 balls, his century in 28 — one ball faster than the previous List A record, Jake Fraser-McGurk's 29-ball hundred for South Australia against Tasmania in 2023 — and 150 in 40 balls, according to ESPNcricinfo. His double century arrived in 52 balls; the record he took belonged to New Zealand's Chad Bowes, who needed 103 balls for Canterbury against Otago in 2024. The International Cricket Council confirmed the marks as List A records, the Associated Press reported.

Twenty-eight of his shots cleared the boundary — the most sixes in a List A innings, passing D'Arcy Short's 23 for Western Australia in 2018 — alongside seven fours, for 196 runs in boundaries and a strike rate of 384.90. He hit four consecutive sixes in the 12th over, and brought up his double century with a six off UAE captain Basil Hameed. Hameed dismissed him in the following over, caught at long-off with India A five runs from the target; Sooryavanshi had scored 204 of the 245 runs on the board when he fell.

"In the previous two games, I got out after getting set."

— Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Player of the Match

The match around him

The UAE, who chose to bat, posted 249 for 8 from their 50 overs, built on Harpreet Singh's 130 off 144 balls, with Basil Hameed adding 36. Arshad Khan was India A's standout bowler with 4 for 43. India A were 108 for 2 after six overs of the chase; Rinku Singh finished unbeaten on 27 as the target fell with 214 balls unused. The full scorecard is on ESPNcricinfo.

A pattern, not a one-off

ESPNcricinfo noted that Sooryavanshi already held the record for the fastest List A fifty before Tuesday. In February he scored 175 in the Under-19 World Cup final as India beat England, he has lit up the Indian Premier League, and earlier this year he became the youngest player to represent India in a full international match, passing a mark held by Sachin Tendulkar, according to the Associated Press. India A's Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign continues in Doha, where Sooryavanshi had already scored heavily in T20 matches last year.
